[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc3Foundations Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The foundations module contains features related to founding and core beliefs/principles of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fnd_ws_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Foundations sidebar lists Churches, Beliefs and the Churches Report. The workspace shows the number of churches and beliefs and a chart of the beliefs added each month.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\u26ea Churches", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Churches list holds your church. Once Enable Multi-Church is switched on in the Multi-Church section of Church Features (click the heading to open it, and click the (i) beside the switch to read what it does), it can also hold branch or satellite churches: mark the main church Is Group, then add each branch with the main church as its Parent Church. There is always exactly one main church (the one without a parent).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1website01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What each church shows on the public website. Tick Publish to put the church on the site, then fill in:
- About and Mission Statement on the About tab, which its About Us page uses
- Image on the Details tab, a photo or logo for its card on the Locations page
- Address, Phone and Email in the Contact section of the Details tab, which the footer and the Contact Us page use
Leave Phone or Email blank and the church shows whatever is in Contact Us Settings, which is shared by the whole site. The Website manual covers how visitors move between locations.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1print001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "These details also print. Anything you print for a branch church, such as a giving statement, carries that church's own name and contact line rather than the main church's. Legal Name and Tax ID work differently: leave them blank on a branch and it prints the main church's, because the main church is usually the registered charity that issues the receipt.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In multi-church mode every church-specific record (Person, Family, Prayer Request, Function, Fund, Collection, Bulletin and so on) gains a Church field, shown near the top of the form and as a standard list filter. New records default to the church of the person saving them. Records that belong to another record (a sign-up to its function, a care request to its person) take that record's church automatically, and a family belongs to the church of its head of household. You can add such a record only for a record of your own church or a shared one: you cannot book another church's room, move money out of its fund, or record a care request, an alms request or a prayer for its people. The Church Directory still lists a family under every branch that has one of its members. Single-church sites never see the field.

Some records can be handed to every church instead of being kept by one. These carry a Shared with all churches tick box: songs, sermons, sermon series and handouts, vendors, rooms, locations and assets, the occasions churches hold together, which are functions and meeting minutes, and the two things money runs through, funds and ministries. Sharing is one record at a time, never a whole type: nothing is shared until somebody ticks the box on that record. Tick it and every church can see and use it, whichever church shared it, and the Church field disappears because the record no longer belongs to one.

Shared By on the record names the church that shared it, and you can filter a list by it to separate what you shared from what was shared with you. Open a record another church shared and a note at the top says so, with the tick box locked.

Only the church that shared a record can stop sharing it, or delete it. Untick the box there and the record goes back to that church and leaves everyone else's lists, and anything attached to it, such as a booking of a shared room, goes back with it. A branch that no longer wants something shared with it has to ask the church that shared it, so one branch cannot take a resource away from the rest. Anything attached to a shared record is shared along with it, such as a booking of a shared room or a sign-up to a shared function, so every church sees the same diary and the same list of names. Gifts and expenses are never shared: each one keeps the church that gave or spent it, so every report shows a church only its own money. A shared fund or ministry therefore shows its joint figures to every church that can see it: the fund's balance and list of transactions, the ministry's running total of what has been spent on it. People and attendance are never shared.

A Budget tracks the spending of its own church. Tick Include Branch Churches on it to count what the churches beneath it spend as well, which is how the main church budgets for everyone at once.

The About tab of the Church record also holds the church's Mission Statement and a Church Verse (a Bible reference, such as John 3:16). It can also carry an Image, such as a logo. Bulletins print the verse on the back cover and the image on the front cover when the Church Verse and Church Image sections are switched on. The Church Directory prints the verse on its cover, and the image as well when Church Image on Cover is ticked. Bulletins and the Church Directory cover print the Website. A branch that leaves Legal Name, Tax ID, Default Bible Translation or Website blank uses its parent's. Tax ID, CCLI License Number, Default Bible Translation and Contact People Only With Their Consent are on the Settings tab.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1f", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turning Enable Multi-Church on stamps the main church on every existing record and gives every existing user a permission for the main church with branches hidden, so nothing becomes visible to anyone by accident. It cannot be turned off again while branch churches exist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1d", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who Sees Which Church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Everyone sees the records of their own church, and nothing from the others. Someone at a branch sees that branch's events, prayer requests and giving. The main church's records stay out of their way, and theirs stay out of the main church's.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "One people directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1dir2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People and families are the exception. Every church can look up every Person and Family, so a branch can find a visitor from the main church, choose a main-church pastor as a counselor or speaker, or check in a family from another campus. The Church field on each person shows which church they belong to.
- Only a person's own church can change them. Another church sees the form as read-only.
- Only a person's own church can add a Background Check, Care Request, Care Assignment or Visitation Log for them. You can open a Follow-up Card only on a Follow-up Workflow of your own church. A workflow that starts by itself, such as on a first check-in, still opens a card for a visitor from another church.
- To move someone to another church, use a Member Transfer.
- Prayer requests, care, counseling, visitation and giving stay with each church, whichever directory setting you use. One exception while the directory is shared: finance and care staff of another church can see a person's Giving and Care figures in lists, reports and exports, but not on the Person form. Check-In, People Editor and Church Manager users of every church can also read a person's Medical Notes. To keep all of these inside each church, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church.

To hide each church's people and families from the other churches, tick Keep People and Families Private to Each Church in Church Features. The Check-In Station still finds everyone at a function that is shared with all churches. Addresses stay readable: Church Manager, Church Staff and Church People Editor users of every church can read every address, and an address is titled with the household or person name.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Where a person's church comes from", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "From the Church field on their Person record. Fill that in, link them to a login (Actions > Invite to Portal does this for you), and they can see that church and no other. There is nothing else to set up.
If they later move to another church, change the same field, or confirm a Member Transfer with a To Church. What they can see moves with them.
A staff login is different. Linking it to a person by hand does not change its churches, so set them in User Permission. A later change of the person's Church field, or a Member Transfer, still moves them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who belong to one church", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Most people. They never have to choose a church, so the app stops asking: the Church field is hidden on their forms, the Church filter is hidden on their lists and reports, and anything they create belongs to their church automatically.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e6", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Seeing the branches as well", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Someone at a church that has branches beneath it still sees only their own church to begin with. To bring the branches in, choose Include Branch Churches from the menu at the top left. While the branches are included:
- a blue note sits at the top of every page, so nobody forgets they are looking at more than their own church
- that same menu item now reads Hide Branch Churches, which puts things back
- lists and reports gain a Church box. Leave it empty to see every church at once, or pick one church to see only that church.
- ticking Expand filters to branches on the blue note changes that last point: picking a church then shows its branches too. This is remembered for that person alone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who see everything", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two kinds of account: the built-in Administrator, which the app never restricts, and anyone who has not been given a church. Their reports still open on the main church, so clear the Church box to see every church at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1share1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Assigning and sharing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1share2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, you can assign a record (Assign To) or share it only with someone who can see that record's church. Assigning it to anyone else stops with a message, because the assignment would let them read a record of another church. A record of one church cannot be shared with everyone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e10", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If someone sees the wrong thing", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Ch1e11", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check the Church field on their Person record first, since that is what drives everything else. What it creates behind the scenes is a User Permission, which an administrator can look at or change there directly. A change made by hand stays until that person's church or login changes, at which point it is set again from their Person record.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Church001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Keep a church away from AI. A church can keep its records and its people away from Churchit's own AI features. Tick Keep This Church Away From AI on the Settings tab of the church (see Keep a church or a person away from AI).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fQeaH6cwov", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note: Without multi-church, only one Church record is allowed. With it, only one main church (a church without a Parent Church) is allowed; every other church must have a Parent Church that is marked Is Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4Beliefs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "rx8sNKF0oc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Beliefs are the foundational principles the church stands for.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nVhOr1yDL4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding church beliefs, note the following:
- Type the Bible references each belief rests on, such as Romans 3:23; Ephesians 2:8-9. They show beneath the statement on the Beliefs web page.
- The Beliefs list and the Beliefs web page show beliefs in the order you added them. The Publish column shows which ones are on the website.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetricsH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc8Weekly Metrics", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Weekly Metrics keeps one record for each church and each week, in the Setup folder of the Summary sidebar. Each record is named by the first day of its week, with the church's abbreviation after it when you have more than one church. It holds the attendance of the week, the first-time visitors, the active members, the people in groups, the people who serve, and the giving and givers of the week. Churchit writes these records itself every night. You cannot add or change one by hand.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each night, Churchit writes this week and counts last week again. So attendance, first-time visitors and giving can change when someone records a late check-in or a late collection. Active members, people in groups and people serving are the counts on the day of the record. Churchit writes them only for the current week, so last week keeps the numbers of its last day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fill the past year. Open Weekly Metrics and click Fill the Last 52 Weeks. Only Church Manager and System Manager users see this button. It fills attendance, first-time visitors and giving for the weeks before last week, and the nightly job writes last week. A week that had no record before shows 0 for members, groups and serving, because Churchit cannot know those numbers for the past. A week that had a record keeps its numbers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the numbers count. Attendance adds the attendance of each function that starts in the week. A function that is shared with all churches counts one time, for the church that shared it. The schedule of a repeating function does not count. Giving adds every submitted collection of the week, the same total as the Weekly Giving chart. It includes sign-up and form payments and refunds. Givers counts each person who gave in the week one time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wkMetrics05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see the giving numbers. Church Staff see the other numbers. The Summary workspace shows the Attendance by Week chart, and Church Finance and Church Manager users also see the Giving by Week chart. If you change the first day of the week in System Settings, new records start on the new day, and the weeks before and after the change overlap.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd17Send records to other systems", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This part is for a System Manager. Churchit can send a record to another system when someone adds or changes it, for example to a mailing tool or a chat room. You do not need custom code.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send a record with a Webhook", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Webhooks and add one:
- Set DocType to the record to send, such as Person, Function Sign-Up or Connection Card. Set Doc Event to when it goes, such as after_insert for a new record.
- Set Request URL to the address that the other system gives you.
- Tick Enable Security and type a Webhook Secret. Give the same secret to the other system. Each request then carries a signature in the X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature header, so the other system can check that the request came from your site.
- Set Request Structure to JSON. In JSON Request Body, put only the fields that the other system needs, for example {\"first_name\": \"{{ doc.first_name }}\", \"email\": \"{{ doc.email }}\"}.
- With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition, with the ID of the church from its Church record. Then only that church's records go.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Send an alert to a chat room", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook06", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe sends alerts to Slack. Mattermost and Matrix accept the same alerts:
- In the chat app, make an incoming webhook and copy its address. In Mattermost this is an Incoming Webhook. In Matrix it is a webhook of the hookshot bridge.
- Find Slack Webhook URL with the search bar, add one with a Name, and paste the address in Webhook URL.
- Open Notifications and add one. Set Channel to Slack, choose the Slack Webhook URL in Slack Channel, and set Document Type, Send Alert On and Message.
- With more than one church, type doc.church == \"CHURCH-ID\" in Condition.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Fdn1hook07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note: Never send care, medical, pickup or giving fields to another system, in a Webhook or in an alert. The other system does not protect them as Churchit does.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHead0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\udd16AI and your church's data", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiIntro001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This part is for a System Manager and a Church Manager. It says what an AI app can do on your site, who can connect one, how to control it, and what Churchit's AI actions do. Frappe changes its AI settings often, so check this part at each Frappe update. Last checked: 6 November 2026, Frappe 16.54, and for Flow the development version of Frappe of that day.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHead0002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turn AI on or off", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiMcp00001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe has an MCP server. An AI app, such as Claude or ChatGPT, signs in to it as one person and works with that person's permissions. Frappe turns it on by default for every site.
Churchit turns it off. Use AI in Churchit in AI Settings (Settings sidebar, Module Settings) is off on a new site and on a site that updated from an older version. While it is off, the MCP server is closed: an AI app gets \"not found\", Enable MCP on the AI Agents tab of System Settings is cleared, System Settings refuses to set it with \"Turn on AI in Church AI Settings first.\", and each update of the site closes it again. MCP is one setting for the whole site, so this also closes MCP for other Frappe apps on the site, such as ERPNext. When the install of Churchit or an update closes MCP, each System Manager gets one notice that names those apps and says how to open MCP again.
To allow AI, a System Manager or a Church Manager reads the warnings on AI Settings (see below), ticks Use AI in Churchit, ticks I Understand What an AI App Can See, Change and Send and saves. The form shows who turned it on and when. With more than one church, only a Church Manager who has no church restriction can turn it on. Any Church Manager can turn it off. Turning it on does not set Enable MCP. A System Manager then ticks it in System Settings. A site that wants MCP for another app, such as ERPNext, turns on AI first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiWarn000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The warnings on AI Settings. A yellow note at the top of the form says what a connected AI app can see, change and send. Below the switch, each part with a title that starts with Warning: explains one risk: what an AI app can see and change, where a hosted AI app sends your data, text that guests and members write, who can use AI, what turning AI off does not stop, and what no switch stops. On a site with Flow, two more parts explain what turning AI on starts in Flow, and Flow knowledge (see Flow knowledge below). These parts start closed. Click a title to open it, and read each one before you turn AI on. On a site without Flow, the form leaves out its sentences about Flow, the two Flow warnings and the Flow Knowledge part.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiMcp00002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Turning AI off closes MCP again and adds a comment to the form. On a site with Flow, it also stops new Flow chats and Flow triggers (see below). It deletes nothing and does not stop API keys. It does not sign out connected apps either: their tokens still work with the REST API. Revoke apps as below.
The AI Access on This Site panel at the foot of AI Settings lists each way AI can reach the site, whether it is on, and a link to the setting that owns it. It also counts the people who may connect an AI app, and lists each app that every desk user may sign in. It also says whether Agent Instructions name the Churchit guide (see Churchit's rules for AI apps). A Church Manager sees \"Ask a System Manager\" for these lines and for connected apps and API keys.
On a site with Flow, the panel also lists who can use Flow, the Flow knowledge sources that read church records and whether their DocType is blocked, the Flow triggers that are on and each one to check, and each AI model with its Privacy Label. The line Churchit AI actions shows the model and the Privacy Label of Writer and Private Work. It turns orange when an AI action would be refused (see Churchit's AI actions in the desk). It also says whether Churchit's agents are ready and whether the Churchit Manual is in Flow knowledge (see Churchit's agents in Flow and Ask the manual). A Church Manager sees \"Ask a System Manager\" for those lines too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHead0007", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What a connected AI app can do", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiCanDo001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An AI app works as the person who connected it. It can see and change everything that person can see and change in the desk. If the person may read care notes, counseling, medical notes, giving or the details of children, the AI app can read them too. It can add, change and delete records and send emails, many in the time a person handles one.
Churchit does not hide records or fields from an AI app and does not stop its changes. The person's own permissions are the limit. So decide who may connect an AI app with care (see the next part).
Ask each person who uses an AI app to keep its setting that asks before every change turned on, and to read each change before they approve it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHead0008", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hosted and local AI models", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHosted01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A hosted AI app, such as Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini, sends everything it reads to the company that runs it. That company keeps and uses the data under its own terms. Read the terms before you turn AI on, and ask the people who use such an app to give it only what a task needs.
A local AI model runs on your own computer, for example in Ollama or LM Studio, and keeps the data on that computer. Prefer a local model for care, counseling, medical and giving records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiHead0003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who can connect an AI app", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiWho00001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Only a Church Manager, a System Manager or a person with the Church AI User role can connect an AI app. Frappe checks this when the person signs in an app that registered itself, because Churchit gives such an app these three roles as its Allowed Roles. Churchit also refuses the MCP server to every other person, whether they come with an app, an API key or their own signed-in session.
To let another person connect an AI app, a System Manager opens the person's User record and adds the Church AI User role under Roles. Give it only to people you trust to send what they can read to an AI company. Church Managers and System Managers need no extra role. The role gives no desk access and opens no record, so it gives a member nothing.
To stop a person, remove the role. The MCP server refuses them at once, but an app that is already connected keeps its token for the REST API. So also delete the person's tokens in OAuth Bearer Token.
An app that a System Manager adds by hand in OAuth Client keeps the Allowed Roles it is given, and one added with none gets the three roles above. Apps that were on the site before this update keep their roles, and Frappe gave many of them every desk user. The AI Access panel lists each app that every desk user may sign in. If it is an AI app, set its Allowed Roles to Church Manager, System Manager and Church AI User.
An API key works without MCP and whether AI is on or not. It gives an AI app or a script the access of the key's owner. Only a System Manager can make a key, so make keys only for people you trust.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiConnH0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Connect your AI app", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiConn00001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "This part is for a System Manager and for the people who connect an AI app. An app that you connect works as you, with your permissions (see above).
1. A Church Manager or a System Manager turns on AI in AI Settings, after the warnings are read.
2. A System Manager ticks Enable MCP on the AI Agents tab of System Settings. Churchit never ticks it.
3. The person who connects an app is a Church Manager, a System Manager, or has the Church AI User role. The Flow User role does not let a person connect an outside app. It lets a person use Flow in the desk.
4. In the app, add a connector, or an MCP server, with this address: https://<your site>/api/v2/mcp. The app opens a Frappe page. The person signs in and approves the app. The app is then connected.
5. Optional. Open the Resource tab of OAuth Settings and set Resource Name to the name of your church, for example \"Grace Church Churchit\". An app shows this name when it asks the person to sign in. The default is \"Frappe Framework Application\". On the Authorization tab, keep Enable Dynamic Client Registration ticked, so that an app can register itself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiConn00002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Apps on 7 November 2026. Apps and plans change often, so read the help of the app again before you rely on this list. We did not test each app. \"Not confirmed\" marks what we read but could not check. For each app, the list gives the plan that you need, the training setting to turn off in your own account, and where your data goes.
- Claude (claude.ai, Claude Desktop and the phone app). Plan: a custom connector works on Free, with one connector, and on Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise. Turn off: Help improve Claude. Data: Anthropic. Anthropic's help page \"Get started with custom connectors using remote MCP\" shows the steps.
- ChatGPT (the web page only). Plan: Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu, with developer mode turned on. It is not on Free and not in the phone app. The pages of OpenAI disagree on which plans can also change records: one says Plus and Pro, another says only Business, Enterprise and Edu (not confirmed). Turn off: Improve the model for everyone. Data: OpenAI.
- Gemini (the web app, with custom apps). Plan: Google AI Pro or Ultra (not confirmed). It needs a personal Google account, not a work or school account. Keep Activity must be on, and we do not know how Google then uses the chats (not confirmed). Turn off: nothing that we know of. Data: Google.
- LM Studio with a local model. Plan: free. Use version 0.4.10 or later, which signs in to an MCP server with OAuth. Turn off: nothing, because the data stays on your computer when the model is local. Data: your computer. Not confirmed: the terms of LM Studio for use at work. If you add the app by hand in OAuth Client, its Redirect URI is http://127.0.0.1:33389/mcp-oauth-callback, and its Allowed Roles are Church Manager, System Manager and Church AI User.
- Open WebUI with a local model. Plan: free. Use version 0.6.31 or later, which signs in with OAuth 2.1. From version 0.6.6 its licence asks you to keep the Open WebUI name when more than 50 people use it in 30 days. Turn off: nothing, when the model is local. Data: your own server.
- Claude Code, on your own computer. Plan: a Claude plan or an Anthropic API key. Add the server with claude mcp add --transport http churchit https://<your site>/api/v2/mcp, the command in the guide of Frappe. Turn off: Help improve Claude, when you use a Claude account. Data: Anthropic.
- frappectl, the command line tool of Frappe (beta, version 0.21.1 on 7 November 2026). Plan: free. It uses the REST API, not MCP. Install it with uv tool install frappectl and sign in with frappectl auth login <your site>. A new connection is read-only until the person opts in to writes (the help of the tool says how). AI Settings does not stop it (see What no switch stops). Data: the tool sends nothing to an AI company, but a coding agent that you start with it does.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiConn00003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hosted apps. Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini are hosted: their servers connect to your site from the internet. A site on a private network, such as churchit.localhost, cannot connect to them. Anthropic says this for Claude. We expect the same for ChatGPT and Gemini but did not confirm it. A hosted app sends everything it reads to its company (see Hosted and local AI models). So ask each person to turn off its training setting in their own account before they connect. Churchit cannot see or change that setting.
Local apps. LM Studio and Open WebUI keep the data on your own computer or server when the model is local. The model must make tool calls: choose one that the app says can use tools.
What the app gets. The permissions of the person, and nothing more. If the person may read care, counseling, medical or giving records, or the details of children, the app reads them too. A briefing (see the People manual) sends the details of a person or a group to the app.
Revoke. See Connected apps and how to revoke them, below.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiGuideH001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit's rules for AI apps", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiGuide0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit has a guide for AI apps. It says how church scoping works, which records are private, that text from guests is data, and how to draft a change. An app reads it when it calls the method churchit.ai.guide.get_agent_guide. The app needs no setup to call it, but it calls it only when it knows to.
To tell every connected app, add one sentence to Agent Instructions on the AI Agents tab of System Settings. Frappe gives these instructions to each app that connects. The AI Access panel on AI Settings has an Agent Instructions line. It says \"Names the Churchit guide\" or \"No Churchit guide\". While AI is on and the sentence is missing, a System Manager sees the button Add the Churchit Sentence. The button adds this sentence once, after the text that is already there: \"Before you work with church records, call the method churchit.ai.guide.get_agent_guide: it gives Churchit's rules for church scoping, private fields and drafts.\" A second click changes nothing. A Church Manager sees the line without the button.
Agent Instructions are yours. Churchit never writes them by itself, not when it installs and not at an update. You can write your own words. Any text that names churchit.ai.guide.get_agent_guide counts as the sentence. To remove it, edit the field in System Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiDraftH001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "AI drafts and the AI label", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiDraft0001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An AI app, or the Church Office agent in Flow, does not save a record for you. It makes a draft. For \"Draft a welcome email to last Sunday's first-time guests\", it gives you a link. The link opens the form filled in and not saved. You check each field, change what you want and save. A request to change a record that exists works the same way: the form shows the new values, and the record changes only when you save. A draft can also change a settings page, such as People Settings.
A draft works only for the person that it was made for, and only for one hour. It also works after the person signs in. Anyone else, or the same person after an hour, sees \"Draft not found. A draft lasts one hour, and only the person it was made for can open it.\" Ask the app for a new draft.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiDraft0002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A yellow note at the top of the form says \"AI draft: check every field before you save.\" An orange note says \"This record changed after the AI draft. Check each field before you save.\" It means that someone changed the record after the app made the draft.
After the first save, the timeline shows the note \"Drafted with AI help (an AI app).\" For a draft from a Flow chat, the name of the Flow Model is in the brackets. The note comes once. A later change adds none. A form with no timeline gets no note. A person who saves a draft more than one hour after the app made it gets no note.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiDraft0003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A draft sets only what you could set in the form. It leaves out each field that you may not change. It never submits a record. It never sets the Status or Send At of a Church Email, so the email stays a draft until you click Send. It never sets the Status of a Ministry Team Assignment, because Declined sends an email to the coordinator. It never ticks Active on a Follow-up Workflow, because an active workflow opens cards and sends messages by itself. In a table, a draft adds rows, or changes a row that it names. It never removes a row. A draft of a cancelled record is refused. An AI app can make 30 drafts an hour for one person.
A draft is the one thing that an AI app gives you and that saves nothing. Still read each field: the app can write a value that looks right and is wrong. Saving a draft does what the same save in the desk does, so some saves send a message. For example, a new Function Sign-Up emails its confirmation.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlowHead01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Flow, Frappe's AI agents", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlow000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Flow is the AI agents feature of Frappe. It is in the development version of Frappe, which becomes Frappe 17. A site on Frappe 16 has no Flow, so this part does not apply to it. In Flow, a person chats with an AI agent in the desk. The agent works with the permissions of that person, like an AI app that connects over MCP. Flow sends what an agent reads to the AI model that a System Manager adds in Flow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlowAssist1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe adds a general assistant agent to Flow, and Churchit has no setting for it. It can read, add, change and delete every record that the person can. While AI is on, a System Manager can turn it off: open the agent frappe/Flow in the Flow Agent list and clear Enabled. Do this right after you turn on AI, because while AI is off a System Manager cannot open an agent. An update keeps this choice. Flow is new and changes often, so check this part at each Frappe update.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlow000002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use AI in Churchit also controls Flow. While it is off, nobody can start a Flow chat or send a new message in an old one. A trigger cannot start a chat, and nobody can add a knowledge source.
Flow lists no agents while AI is off. A person with the Flow User role sees \"Ask an administrator to enable an agent.\" A System Manager sees \"Every model is set, but no agent is enabled.\" and an Enable an agent button. Both messages can mean that AI is off. Turn on AI in AI Settings. Do not enable agents while AI is off. A person can still open their own old chat to read it. Flow then says that only the owner can send messages in it, and the owner is that person. This also means that AI is off.
The chat button of Flow stays on the screen for people who can use Flow. Frappe adds it, and Churchit cannot hide it.
Administrator is the one exception. Frappe gives Administrator every right, so Administrator can continue a chat that already exists. Never use Flow as Administrator.
Turning AI off does not stop a reply that Flow is writing at that moment, and after that only Administrator can stop it. So to stop a reply that changes records, first clear Enabled on its agent in the Flow Agent list. Flow checks it before the agent uses each tool. Then turn AI off. The steps for when AI got it wrong, below, give this order.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlow000003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who can use Flow. A person with the Flow User role can chat with Flow agents in the desk. Frappe makes this role, and Churchit adds no role. A System Manager gives it on the person's User record. A System Manager can also use Flow without it. Give the role only to people you trust to send what they can read to an AI company.
Flow does not use the Church AI User role. That role, with Church Manager and System Manager, lets a person connect an outside AI app (see above). The Flow User role does not give that right. The AI Access panel counts the people who can use Flow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlow000004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Ask before every change. Each Flow chat has an Approval Mode, which the person picks in the chat. In Ask (called Ask for approval in the chat), the agent stops at every change and asks the person. In Auto, a second AI model approves the changes that the person asked for, and the agent asks the person about the rest. In Auto-approve, the agent makes every change without asking.
Flow starts a new chat in Auto. Churchit starts a new chat that a person opens in Ask instead. Before the first message, the picker of a new chat shows Auto, but the chat starts in Ask. A person can change the mode of a chat. To use Auto, change it after the first message. Ask each person to keep Ask and to read each change before they approve it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiOfficeH01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit's agents in Flow", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiOffice001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a site with Flow, Churchit adds three agents to the Flow Agent list: Church Office, Writer and Private Work. Their names are churchit/Church Office, churchit/Writer and churchit/Private Work. An agent needs an AI model, so Churchit adds them only after a System Manager saves an enabled chat model in Flow. An embedding model does not count. Churchit adds the agents again when a chat model is saved, in a background job when AI is turned on, and at each update. Until then, Flow lists none of them, and the AI Access panel says \"Not ready\" for Churchit agents in Flow.
Each agent starts on the oldest enabled chat model. A System Manager can change the Model of an agent in the Flow Agent form, and an update keeps the choice. Nothing else on these agents can be changed, because Flow locks the agents that an app adds.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiOffice002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church Office is the agent for your staff. A person opens the panel of Flow (Ctrl+I, or Cmd+I on a Mac) and picks Church Office. It answers with the permissions of the person: it sees what the person sees in the desk and nothing more. It never saves a record. For a new record or a change, it gives a draft link (see AI drafts above), and the person opens it and saves.
Church Office answers the questions of the weekly office work (see Lists of People in the People manual). These are first-time guests with no follow-up, people not seen lately, birthdays and anniversaries, groups that need attention, open team positions, and what needs the attention of the person this week. It makes a smart list from a sentence and briefs the person on a person or a group. It reads and describes records, runs reports, reads the page that is open beside the chat, reads the guide of Churchit and searches the manual (see Ask the manual). It has no web search, no memory and no tool that creates, changes or deletes a record. A chat with it starts in Ask, but none of its tools asks, because none changes data. Each briefing is kept in the Access Log.
Flow lets you share a chat with a person, or open it to every Flow User. They then see what Church Office read with your permissions, also what they may not read in the desk. Do not share a chat that holds a briefing or other private records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiOffice003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Writer and Private Work have no tools. Churchit's AI actions use them (see Churchit's AI actions in the desk), and nobody can chat with them in Flow. Set the Model of Private Work to one whose Privacy Label is Zero retention or Local (see Choose an AI provider for Flow).
Roles on an agent. A System Manager can set Roles on each Churchit agent in the Flow Agent form. Only people with one of those roles can use the agent. An agent with no roles is open to every Flow User, and a System Manager can use every agent. An update keeps the roles. Roles do not change what a person can read, because the agent works with the permissions of the person. Use them to limit who may chat with Church Office, for example to your staff.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiOffice004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose a model for Church Office. Church Office needs a model that makes tool calls. On 7 November 2026 we tried qwen2.5-coder (3B and 7B) and granite3.2 (2B) in Ollama 0.34. Each chose the right tool but wrote the call as text, so Flow ran no tool and the answer was the call itself. On a computer with no large graphics card, a 7B model took more than five minutes for one answer, which is longer than Flow waits. Put {\"timeout\": 1500, \"num_ctx\": 16384} in Extra Params on the Flow Model to let it finish. The first request of a Church Office chat is about 3,000 tokens, and a briefing can add several thousand more. Without num_ctx, Ollama can use a shorter context, such as 4,096 tokens, and cut the rest. We did not try a hosted model, or another local model, with Church Office, so we do not know which works best. Test the model that you choose with a plain question before your staff use it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit's AI actions in the desk", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a site with Flow, Churchit adds buttons to the desk that ask an AI model for a draft or a summary. The other manuals say where each button is and what it does: Describe People, Brief Me, Draft Note With AI, Suggest Mapping and Describe the Process (People manual), Find Action Items (Operations manual), Draft with AI (Communications manual), Study with AI (Study manual), Describe the Form (Ministries manual) and Alt Text with AI (Website manual). Explain, on a report, is in this manual. This part says what all of them share.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who sees a button. A button shows only when AI is on in AI Settings, Flow is ready (see Churchit's agents in Flow) and you may use the agent that the button needs. You may use an agent when you are a System Manager, or when you have the Flow User role and the agent has no Roles, or one of your roles is in its Roles. Most buttons need Writer. Draft Note With AI and Find Action Items need Private Work too. For another button that sends a private record, Flow refuses the request when you may not use Private Work. On a site without Flow, and while AI is off, no button shows.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which agent and which model. An action sends its request to the Writer agent. When the request holds a record of a DocType in the Private Records list (see below), it goes to Private Work instead. Churchit reads the Privacy Label of the model of that agent (see Choose an AI provider for Flow) and refuses the request when the label is too weak:
- A request with no church record runs on any label. It holds only text that you typed, text that the church publishes, field labels and choices, or the names of groups, ministries and skills.
- A request with church records needs No training, Zero retention or Local.
- A request with a record of a DocType in the Private Records list needs Zero retention or Local.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000005", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What each button needs.
- Any label: Describe People, Draft with AI, Describe the Form, Describe the Process, Suggest Mapping, and Study with AI on the notes of a published sermon.
- No training, Zero retention or Local: Brief Me, Explain on a report, Study with AI on a sermon that is not published or that has a Transcript, and Draft with AI on a Function that is not published.
- Zero retention or Local: Draft Note With AI, Find Action Items, Explain on a finance report, and Brief Me or Explain when the request holds a record of a DocType in the Private Records list, such as a visit, a note, a care request or a gift. Brief Me on a person holds a gift, a care request or a background check when you may see the giving, care or background check fields of the person.
These levels follow the recommended Private Records list. When you change the list, the level of a button changes with it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000006", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When Churchit refuses an action. The dialog closes and a message says why. For a label that is too weak, it reads, for example: \"Note draft needs a model labelled Zero retention or Local, but the model of the churchit/Private Work agent is labelled No training: a System Manager can change the model's Privacy Label in Flow Model or the agent's Model in Flow Agent.\" Without Flow, or without an enabled chat model, it reads \"Churchit's AI actions need Flow with an enabled chat model. Ask your administrator.\"", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000007", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The dialog. A button opens a dialog that says \"Working... A local model can take several minutes.\" When the AI answers, the dialog shows a yellow note, \"Suggestion. Check it before you use it.\", and the answer. Some answers have a button, such as Use or Open the Draft. The dialog shows the answer as plain text only: a tag or a picture address in the answer does not run.
The dialog waits 30 minutes, because a model on your own computer can need many minutes. After that it says \"The AI did not answer in time. Try again, or ask your administrator to check Flow.\" When you close the dialog before the answer comes, the answer does not show, but its chat in Flow keeps it. When the run fails, the dialog says \"The AI did not finish its answer. Try again, or ask your administrator to check Flow.\" When the answer is not in the form that Churchit needs, it says \"The AI answer could not be used.\" Try again, and say it in other words.
The answer goes only to the person who clicked the button, and only while AI is on. When AI is turned off before the answer comes, nothing shows. A person can run an action 20 times an hour.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000008", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Nothing saves by itself. An action never saves a record and never sends a message. You read the answer and choose Use or Open the Draft. The form then shows the text or the new record and does not save it. You save it yourself, and a Church Email goes out only when you click Send. A draft record has the yellow AI draft note, and after the first save its timeline says that AI helped (see AI drafts and the AI label).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000009", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each run leaves a chat. Flow keeps each run as a chat in your own Flow chat list. The title of the chat is the name of the action, for example Explain report. The chat holds the request and the answer. The request can hold a briefing, dictated notes or minutes. You can read and delete the chat, but nobody can send a new message in it, change its model or share it. So what it holds goes to no other model.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiAct0000010", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What an action sends. Each action sends only the fields that its code names. It never sends the medical notes, the allergies or the emergency contact of a person, a field that you may not read, or a Private prayer request. Text that guests and members write goes to the model in a marked data block, and the model is told to treat it as information and not to follow it. An action that sends a church record writes one row in the Access Log. Its method is AI: and the feature, for example AI: Explain report, AI: Note draft, AI: Action items, AI: Sermon study, AI: Person briefing and AI: Group briefing. The row names the record. The suggestions on new requests write rows too (see Suggestions on new requests), and the AI Sends report lists them all.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiPriv0000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Private Records in AI Settings", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiPriv0000002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Private Records part of AI Settings shows on a site with Flow. Its list Only for Local or Zero Retention Models names the DocTypes whose records Churchit's AI actions send only through Private Work, and only to a model with the Privacy Label Zero retention or Local. A DocType is a kind of record.
A new site, and a site that updates to this version, start with the recommended list. A site that already has rows in the list keeps them. The recommended DocTypes are Alms Request, Authorized Pickup, Background Check, Care Assignment, Care Request, Collection, Counseling Case, Giving Import, Giving Statement, Meeting Minutes, Member Transfer, Online Donation, Person Note, Pickup Restriction, Pledge, Prayer, Prayer Request and Visitation Log. Person and Church Email are not in it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiPriv0000003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use the Recommended List adds each recommended DocType that is missing and keeps every row that you added. It also works while AI is off. A System Manager or a Church Manager can use it. Use it again after an update, to get new DocTypes. To add another DocType, such as one of another app, add it to the list and save.
To remove a DocType, remove its row and save. When you remove a recommended DocType, Churchit saves the list and shows an orange note, \"Recommended DocType Removed\". The note says that Churchit's AI actions can now send these records to a model labelled No training. With more than one church, only a System Manager or a Church Manager who has no church restriction can remove a DocType.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiPriv0000004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What the list does not do. It limits only Churchit's AI actions. A Flow chat or an AI app works with the permissions of the person and sends what it reads, whatever the list says (see What a connected AI app can do). The list is not Blocked from Flow Knowledge, which stops Flow knowledge sources (see Flow knowledge). When a DocType is gone from the site, the next update removes its row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiExpl0000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Explain a report with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiExpl0000002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A script report of Churchit has the menu item Explain. Open the report, set its filters, click the menu (the three dots at the top right) and choose Explain. The dialog shows a short summary of the rows, the trend when the AI sees one, and up to three questions to ask next. Beside them it shows the rows that the AI got, for example \"The AI got 2 of 2 rows.\" When the answer has a number that is in no row, the dialog says \"These numbers are not in the rows: ...\" so that you can check it.
Churchit runs the report again as you, with the filters on the screen. So the report roles, the report permission and the churches that you may see apply as in the desk. The AI gets the columns and at most 200 rows. It never gets a field that you may not read, or the medical notes, allergies and emergency contacts of a person. A report on records of a DocType in the Private Records list, such as a giving report, goes to Private Work.
The item does not show on a Report Builder report. It never shows on Active Prayer List, Children, Church Directory Report, Person Birthdays This Month, Person Birthdays This Week, Pastoral Care Watch List, Prayer Requests Recently Answered and Prayer Requests Recently Created, because they are about children, list the names, ages or birthdays of children, or can hold Private prayer requests. Churchit refuses them too. When a church that you may read keeps away from AI, Explain refuses a report that can hold its rows. In the Church filter, pick a church that does not keep away. A report with no Church filter is refused while one of your churches keeps away. The run is kept in the Access Log as AI: Explain report, with the report and its filters.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Suggestions on new requests", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a site with Flow, Churchit can suggest the next step for a new request. The person who reads the suggestion first is the reviewer. Suggestions are off. A Church Manager or a System Manager ticks Suggest Next Steps on New Requests in the Suggestions on New Requests part of AI Settings and adds a reviewer for each church. The part shows only on a site with Flow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which requests. A new Prayer Request, a new Care Request, and a new Follow-up Card that a Connection Card or a form started. A Prayer Request that is Private never gets a suggestion. A record that a Data Import adds gets none. A record of a church that keeps away from AI, or about a person who keeps out, gets none (see Keep a church or a person away from AI). Nothing is sent when AI is off or the church or the person opts out before the job runs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The reviewers. The Reviewers table has a row for each church, with the Church and the Reviewer (a user). A site with one church needs one row, and Church can stay empty. Each church has one reviewer. A church with no row gets no suggestion, and Churchit shows no error. The reviewer must be an enabled desk user who may read the Prayer Requests, Care Requests, Follow-up Cards and AI suggestions of that church and select a Prayer Request Type, a Care Request Type and a Follow-up Workflow, for example a Church Pastoral Care user. When a permission is missing, the message names the DocType. The reviewer must also be allowed to use the agent that the request needs (see Churchit's AI actions in the desk). When a reviewer is disabled, an orange note says so each time you save AI Settings. Choose another reviewer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00005", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who can change it. With more than one church, only a System Manager, or a Church Manager with no church restriction, can turn suggestions on or change the reviewers.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00006", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "How it runs. Nothing goes to a model while the guest or the member saves the request. A moment later, a background job starts the AI run as the reviewer. A local model can take several minutes. The run is a chat in the reviewer's Flow chat list, titled Prayer request suggestions, Care request suggestions or Follow-up suggestions. Only the reviewer reads it, and nobody can continue it or share it. The chat keeps the text of each request and the answer of the AI until Log Settings removes it (Frappe keeps a Flow Session for 90 days). To keep them for less time, open Log Settings and set a shorter time for Flow Session. The run writes a row in the Access Log: AI: Prayer request suggestions, AI: Care request suggestions or AI: Follow-up suggestions. A card from a Connection Card also writes a row for the Connection Card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00007", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which model. A suggestion for a Prayer Request or a Care Request goes to Private Work, because both are in the Only for Local or Zero Retention Models list. Its model needs the Privacy Label Zero retention or Local. A suggestion for a Follow-up Card goes to Writer, and needs No training, Zero retention or Local. When the label is too weak, Churchit sends nothing and the guest or the member sees no message. Use Check the Models to see the label and a result.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00008", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A prayer request. Only Church Pastoral Care, Church Manager and System Manager users see the part AI Suggestion at the top of a Prayer Request. The suggestion is a record of its own, a Church AI Suggestion, so the person who asked, the prayer team and staff with other roles never see it, also not on the website. It shows the Suggested Type, Suggested as Urgent, Flags and Suggested Wording. The flags are Possible risk of harm, Names someone else, Health details, Contact details, Possible spam and Needs a person. Needs a person means that the AI was not sure, or that its answer could not be used. The AI Suggestion menu on the form has Use Type, Use Urgency and Copy Wording. Use Type and Use Urgency put the suggestion in the form and do not save it. Copy Wording copies the wording, and the request keeps its own text. Nothing changes until you save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00009", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The risk flag. Possible risk of harm means possible harm to the person or to other people. Churchit then assigns the AI Suggestion, not the request, at once to each Church Pastoral Care user of its church who may read both. The To Do says \"Read this prayer request now.\" and gives no reason. It opens the AI Suggestion, which has the reason and the button Open Request. The prayer team, staff with other roles and the person who asked see no assignment on the request. Frappe sends its own assignment notice. The flag Needs a person assigns nobody.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00010", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A care request. The part AI Suggestion at the top of a Care Request shows the Suggested Category and the Suggested Urgency to the same three roles. The buttons Use Category and Use Urgency put a value in the form and do not save it. Churchit offers only a category that the reviewer may read. The suggestion shows on the form, not on the Care Board card. Choosing the caregiver stays your step.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00011", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A follow-up card. On a card that a Connection Card or a form started, AI adds the comment AI suggestion. It says which Follow-up Workflow fits, why, and a first email. The comment says \"Check it before you use it. Nothing was sent.\" The button Draft the Email (for users who may create a Church Email) opens a new Church Email that is not saved, for the person of the card, from the latest comment that the reviewer of the card's church added. It goes out only when you read it and click Send. For a card from a form, Churchit sends only the reason of the card and never the answers. The email keeps only {{ first_name }}, {{ last_name }}, {{ display_name }} and {{ full_name }}. A link to another site shows as [link removed].", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Sugg00012", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What AI never does. AI never replies to a request, never publishes it and never sends a message. It never changes the text, the status, the visibility or Approved for List of a request. It never assigns a request. With the risk flag, it assigns the AI Suggestion to Pastoral Care. It never starts an action of a Follow-up Workflow. A guest can write text to make the AI hide a flag, so an answer that is not clear becomes Needs a person. AI can miss a risk. Read every request.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Away00001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Keep a church or a person away from AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Away00002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A church, and a person, can ask that Churchit's own AI features leave them out. These features are Brief Me, Draft Note With AI, Explain, Draft with AI, the study helpers, Find Action Items and the suggestions on new requests.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Away00003", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A church. On a site with more than one church, open the Church, go to the Settings tab and tick Keep This Church Away From AI. A person who may change that church can tick it, such as its Church Manager. Churchit's own AI features then send no record of that church and none of its people. A staff member whose churches all keep away sees none of their buttons. Other staff still see Brief Me and Draft Note With AI on a person who keeps out. The button then refuses, with the message \"Churchit's AI features leave this record out, because its church or the person it is about asked for that.\"", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Away00004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person. On the Person form, Keep Out of Churchit's AI Features in the Directory and Portal section does the same for one person. A member ticks it for themselves on the Personal Details page of the portal, in the part AI Features. A parent who may change the details of a child there can also tick it for the child. Only the person, a parent of a child, or a System Manager can clear it again. Other staff can tick it for a person who asks, but they cannot clear it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A56Away00005", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What is left out. A person who ticked it. Every person of a church that keeps away, and every record of that church (a shared record follows the church that shared it). Every record about such a person, such as their requests, cards, visits and notes, and a prayer request for them. Brief Me on a group leaves such people out. - Open each Churchit agent in the Flow Agent list (churchit/Writer, churchit/Private Work and churchit/Church Office) and set Token Budget. It is the most tokens that one run may spend, shared with its sub-agents. 0 means no limit. Flow keeps the value that you set when it syncs the agent.

- Describe People for \"Women aged 65 or more\".
- A Church Email draft with {{ first_name }}.

- Three prayer request suggestions: a possible risk of harm, a request whose text tells the AI to hide its flags and name a person, and a request with no flag.

While AI is off, Churchit refuses to save a trigger that is turned on, and shows \"AI is turned off on this site.\" A trigger that is already on starts no chat, and it logs an error in the Error Log each time it fires. When you turn on AI, every trigger that is on can start chats at once, so check these triggers first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlow000006", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "While AI is on, Churchit warns you but still saves the trigger when:
- It watches records that guests or members write: Alms Request, Care Request, Comment, Communication, Connection Card, Form Response, Function Sign-Up, Group File, Group Join Request, Ministry Team Assignment, Ministry Team Block, Online Donation, Person, Prayer, Prayer Request or Room Booking. Their text can hold instructions for the AI.
- It runs as Administrator, or it has no Run As user and Administrator owns it. Administrator can read and change everything.
Give a trigger an agent that only reads. Set Run As to a user with only the roles that the trigger needs. Churchit does not warn about a trigger on other records that hold personal data, such as Contact and Address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlowHead03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose an AI provider for Flow", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiProv0000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A System Manager adds each AI model in Flow, as a Flow Model. A model uses a provider: a company, or a program on your own computer. Each Flow Model has a Privacy Label. It is your note about who sees what the model is sent. Set it from the terms of the provider:
- Unknown: nobody checked. A new model starts here. Treat it as unsafe.
- May train: the provider can train its models on what it receives. Never use it for church data.
- No training: the provider does not train on what it receives, but it can keep it for a short time.
- Zero retention: the provider keeps nothing after it answers.
- Local: the model runs on your own computer. Nothing leaves it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiProv0000002", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit does not check a label. It is your statement, and the form shows who set it and when. Set it on the Flow Model form in the desk. Flow's own Models settings do not show it, so open each model from the AI Access panel. The panel lists each enabled model with its label and warns about Unknown and May train. Flow sends a model what a chat reads, whatever the label says. So set the label before anyone uses the model. Providers change their terms often, so read them again before you rely on this list. DPA means data processing agreement.
- A model on your own computer, such as Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp. Put its address in Base URL. Label: Local. You need no DPA. For tool use, pick a model that fits 16 GB of video memory or more. Ollama has no sign-in, so protect it with a key if it runs on another computer.
- Cloudflare Workers AI, the free daily allowance. Label: Zero retention. Cloudflare says it does not train on the data or keep it. Keep AI Gateway logging off. The Free plan stops at the daily allowance. Cloudflare has a DPA, so check that it covers your plan.
- Groq, with Zero Data Retention turned on in its Data Controls. Label: Zero retention. Groq has a DPA. Its free limits are small and change often. Without that setting, leave the label on Unknown.
- OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini, with billing turned on. Label: No training. They keep data for a short time to check for abuse. Each has a DPA. Ask OpenAI for it on its enterprise privacy page. Anthropic includes it in its Commercial Terms. Google offers it for paid use only.
- Mistral, with billing turned on. Label: No training only after you turn off training in your Mistral account. Until then, use May train. Mistral has a DPA for commercial customers, so check that it covers your use.
- OpenRouter, with routing limited to providers with Zero Data Retention (put {\"provider\": {\"zdr\": true}} in Extra Params on the Flow Model). Label: Zero retention. Without that, turn off training for paid models in your OpenRouter privacy settings and use No training. OpenRouter has a DPA in its terms. The provider behind OpenRouter sets its own terms.
- Free tiers that train: the Gemini API free tier, Mistral free, OpenRouter models with :free in the name, and the NVIDIA build trial. Label: May train. Never use them for church data. Google allows only its paid Gemini service for people in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland.
- Frappe Cloud AI credits. Label: Unknown. - OpenAI: Organization limits, Spend, Edit spend limit. Tick Enforce a hard limit. Without it, the limit only sends alerts.
- Anthropic: Console, Billing, Spend limits, Set limit.
- Gemini: AI Studio, Spend, Monthly spend cap.
- Mistral: Admin Panel, Subscriptions, Billing, monthly spending limit.
- Groq: Console, Settings, Billing, Limits, Add Limit.
- OpenRouter: set a Key limit with a monthly reset on each API key.
- Cloudflare: stay on the Free plan, which stops at the daily allowance.
The consoles change their names, so use the help pages of the provider if a name differs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiFlowHead04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Flow knowledge", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiKnow0000001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Flow Knowledge Base holds text that an agent can search. A Flow Knowledge Source with the Source Type DocType fills it with records. A DocType is a kind of record, such as Person or Donation. Flow copies each record of the source's Reference DocType that matches its Filters, with the fields in its Content Fields, and it does not check who may read each record. Anyone who can use an agent that has the knowledge base can read the copied text, whatever their own access to the records. A chat and an AI app work with the person's own permissions, but a knowledge base does not. Flow also sends the copied text to the embedding model that is set in Flow, and copies the changed records again at each sync, each day when Auto Sync is on.
So Churchit blocks the records that hold data about people. Blocked from Flow Knowledge, in the Flow Knowledge part of AI Settings, lists the DocTypes that a knowledge source may not read. A new site, and a site that updates to this version, start with the recommended list: the Churchit records about people, such as Person, Family, Prayer Request, Counseling Case, Counseling Session and Donation, and Frappe's Access Log, Activity Log, Address, Comment, Communication, Contact, Data Import Log, Deleted Document, Email Group Member, Email Queue, Error Log, Event, File, Notification Log, ToDo, User and Version, with their child tables, such as Contact Email and Contact Phone. On a site with Flow, it also holds Flow's own records of chats and knowledge, which keep what each person read with their own permissions: Flow Agent Memory, Flow Knowledge Chunk, Flow Run, Flow Session, Flow Session Attachment and Flow Session Message. Churchit refuses to save a new source on a DocType in the list, or a change that makes a source read one. The message tells the person why. This holds at all times. If another app tries to add such a source when the site updates, Churchit refuses it there too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AiKnow0000004", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A System Manager or a Church Manager can remove a DocType from the list or add any DocType, then save.
